desc:
Find the longest path in a binary tree in which every node has the same value. The path may start and end at any nodes, may pass through the root or not, and can turn at a node (go up to a common ancestor and then down again). Return its length measured in edges, so a path of a single node has length 0. The empty tree also gives 0.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree on the left: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For tree = [5, 4, 5, 1, 1, -1, 5] the answer is 2: the three 5s at the root, its right child and that child's right child form a path with two edges.
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: Look at the highest node of the best path (the place where it turns). It extends down on at most two sides.
For each node compute chain[v]: the longest downward run of equal values that starts at v. A child only extends the chain if it has the same value as v.

The best path that turns at v has length (left run) + (right run), where a run is chain[child] + 1 if the child equals v and 0 otherwise. Take the maximum over all nodes, and set chain[v] to the larger of the two runs.
editorial: Every path has a highest node. If the path is all one value x and peaks at node v with value x, then it goes down into the left child (only if that child also holds x) and down into the right child (same condition), as far as the equal values continue.

Let chain[v] be the number of edges of the longest downward path from v in which all values equal v's value. For the left child a, the run on the left side is chain[a] + 1 when val[a] == val[v] and 0 otherwise; the right side is analogous. Then chain[v] = max(leftRun, rightRun) and the longest path peaking at v has leftRun + rightRun edges. The answer is the maximum of that over all nodes.
In the level-order array, children come after their parents, so processing the real nodes from the last to the first computes all chain values bottom-up without recursion. O(n) time and O(n) space.
solution:
NUL = -1

def _links(t):
    """vals[k], left[k], right[k] for the k-th real node in level order (-1 = no child)."""
    pos, c = [], 0
    for x in t:
        if x == NUL:
            pos.append(-1)
        else:
            pos.append(c)
            c += 1
    vals = [x for x in t if x != NUL]
    left, right = [-1] * c, [-1] * c
    for k in range(c):
        a = 2 * k + 1
        if a < len(t):
            left[k] = pos[a]
        if a + 1 < len(t):
            right[k] = pos[a + 1]
    return vals, left, right


def longestUnivaluePath(tree):
    vals, left, right = _links(tree)
    n = len(vals)
    chain = [0] * n
    best = 0
    for k in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        a, b = left[k], right[k]
        la = chain[a] + 1 if a != -1 and vals[a] == vals[k] else 0
        lb = chain[b] + 1 if b != -1 and vals[b] == vals[k] else 0
        chain[k] = max(la, lb)
        best = max(best, la + lb)
    return best
